#### Index input

The counter can be reset by an index signal coming from the encoder, indicating an absolute reference position. The index signal must be connected to the tim\_etr\_in input. It can be filtered using the digital input filter.

The index functionality is enabled with the IE bit in the TIMx\_ECR register. The IE bit must be set only in encoder mode, when the SMS[3:0] bitfield has the following values: 0001, 0010, 011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111.

Available encoders are proposed with several options for index pulse conditioning, as per [Figure 438](#XREF_47987__Figure_199__Index_gating_options41):

- Gated with A and B: the pulse width is 1/4 of one channel period, aligned with both A and B edges.
- Gated with A (or gated with B): the pulse width is 1/2 of one channel period, aligned with the two edges on channel A (resp. channel B).
- Ungated: the pulse width is up to one channel period, without any alignment to the edges.
<a id="XREF_47987__Figure_199__Index_gating_options41"></a>

#### Figure 438. Index gating options![](MSv45765V1.svg)

The circuitry tolerates jitter on index signal, whatever the gating mode, as shown on [Figure 439](#XREF_65150__Figure_193_41).

In ungated mode, the signal must be strictly below two encoder periods. If the pulse width is greater or equal to two encoder period, the counter is reset multiple times.

<a id="XREF_65150__Figure_193_41"></a>

#### Figure 439. Jittered Index signals![](MSv45766V1.svg)

The timer supports the three gating options identically, without any specific programming needed. It is only necessary to define on which encoder state (for example channel A and channel B state combination) the index must be synchronized, using the IPOS[1:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_ECR register.

The index detection event acts differently depending on counting direction to ensure symmetrical operation during speed reversal:

- The counter is reset during up-counting (DIR bit = 0).
- The counter is set to TIMx\_ARR when down-counting.

This allows the index to be generated on the very same mechanical angular position whatever the counting direction. [Figure 440](#XREF_69382_0%5D%13=_1141) shows at which position is the index generated, for a simplistic example (an encoder providing four edges par mechanical rotation).

<a id="XREF_69382_0%5D%13=_1141"></a>

#### Figure 440. Index generation for IPOS[1:0] = 11![](MSv45767V1.svg)

[Figure 441](#XREF_52830__Figure_190__Counter_reading_with_index_gated_on_channel_A41) presents waveforms and corresponding values for IPOS[1:0] = 11. It shows that the instant at which the counter value is forced is automatically adjusted depending on the counting direction:

- Counter set to 0 when encoder state is 11 (ChA = 1, ChB = 1), when up-counting (DIR bit = 0).
- Counter set to TIMx\_ARR when exiting the 11 state, when down-counting (DIR bit = 1).

An interrupt can be issued upon index detection event.

The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event interrupt generated.

<a id="XREF_52830__Figure_190__Counter_reading_with_index_gated_on_channel_A41"></a>

#### Figure 441. Counter reading with index gated on channel A (IPOS[1:0] = 11)![](MSv45768V1.svg)

[Figure 442](#XREF_31732__Figure_191__Counter_reading_with_index_ungated41) presents waveforms and corresponding values for the ungated mode. The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event generated.

<a id="XREF_31732__Figure_191__Counter_reading_with_index_ungated41"></a>

#### Figure 442. Counter reading with index ungated (IPOS[1:0] = 00)![](MSv45769V1.svg)

[Figure 443](#XREF_69040__Figure_192_41) shows how the gated on A & B mode is handled, for various pulse alignment scenarios. The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event generated.

<a id="XREF_69040__Figure_192_41"></a>

#### Figure 443. Counter reading with index gated on channel A and B![](MSv45770V1.svg)

[Figure 444](#XREF_73550__Figure_194__Narrow_index_pulse_following_a_detection_on_Channel_B41) and [Figure 445](#XREF_42832__Figure_196__Counter_reset_Narrow_index_pulse_(closer_view)41) detail the case where the subsequent index pulse may be narrower than one quarter of the encoder clock period.

<a id="XREF_73550__Figure_194__Narrow_index_pulse_following_a_detection_on_Channel_B41"></a>

#### Figure 444. narrow index pulse (IPOS[1:0] = 11)Encoder mode behavior in case of ![](MSv45771V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_42832__Figure_196__Counter_reset_Narrow_index_pulse_(closer_view)41"></a>

#### Figure 445. Counter reset Narrow index pulse (closer view, ARR = 0x07)![](MSv45772V1.svg)

[Figure 446](#XREF_92120__Figure_197__Index_behavior_in_x1_and_x2_mode41) shows how the index is managed in x1 and x2 modes.

<a id="XREF_92120__Figure_197__Index_behavior_in_x1_and_x2_mode41"></a>

#### Figure 446. Index behavior in x1 and x2 mode (IPOS[1:0] = 01)![](MSv45773V1.svg)

#### Directional index sensitivity

The IDIR[1:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_ECR register allows the index to be active only in a selected counting direction.

[Figure 447](#XREF_24064__Figure_197__Directional_index_sensitivity41) shows the relationship between index and counter reset events, depending on IDIR[1:0] value.

**Note:**

The IDR[1:0] bitfield must be written when IE bit is reset (index mode disabled).

The directional index sensitivity is not supported in clock + direction mode. When SMS[3:0] = 1010 or 1011, the IDIR[1:0] must be set to 00.

<a id="XREF_24064__Figure_197__Directional_index_sensitivity41"></a>

#### Figure 447. Directional index sensitivity![](MSv45774V1.svg)

#### Special first index event management

The FIDX bit in the TIMx\_ECR register allows the index to be taken only once, as shown on [Figure 448](#XREF_10344__Figure_198__Counter_reset_as_function_of_FIDX_bit_setting41). Once the first index has arrived, any subsequent index is ignored. If needed, the circuitry can be rearmed by writing the FIDX bit to 0 and setting it again to 1.

**Note:**

When FIDX = 1, the index can be issued twice (IDXF flag set) if the direction changes at position 0 (index active).

<a id="XREF_10344__Figure_198__Counter_reset_as_function_of_FIDX_bit_setting41"></a>

#### Figure 448. Counter reset as function of FIDX bit setting![MSv45775V1](MSv45775V1.svg)

#### Index management in nonquadrature mode

[Figure 449](#XREF_81356__Figure_201__Index_behavior_in_clock_+_direction_mode41) and [Figure 450](#XREF_24012__Figure_202__Index_behavior_in_directional_clock_mode41) detail how the index is managed in directional clock mode and clock plus direction mode, when the SMS[3:0] bitfield is equal to 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101.

For both of these modes, the index sensitivity is set with the IPOS[0] bit as following:

- IPOS[0] = 0: Index is detected on clock low level.
- IPOS[0] = 1: Index is detected on clock high level.

The IPOS[1] bit is not-significant.

<a id="XREF_81356__Figure_201__Index_behavior_in_clock_+_direction_mode41"></a>

#### Figure 449. Index behavior in clock + direction mode, IPOS[0] = 1![](MSv45777V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_24012__Figure_202__Index_behavior_in_directional_clock_mode41"></a>

#### Figure 450. Index behavior in directional clock mode, IPOS[0] = 1![](MSv45778V1.svg)

#### Encoder error management

For encoder configurations where two quadrature signals are available, it is possible to detect transition errors. The reading on the two inputs corresponds to a 2-bit gray code which can be represented as a state diagram, on [Figure 451](#XREF_76719__Figure_2__State_diagram_for_quadrature_encoded_signals41). A single bit is expected to change at once. An erroneous transition sets the TERRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. A transition error interrupt is generated if the TERRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

<a id="XREF_76719__Figure_2__State_diagram_for_quadrature_encoded_signals41"></a>

#### Figure 451. State diagram for quadrature encoded signals![](MSv45779V1.svg)

For encoder having an index signal, it is possible to detect abnormal operation resulting in an excess of pulses per revolution. An encoder with N pulses per revolution provides 4xN counts per revolution. The index signal resets the counter every 4xN clock periods.

If the counter value is incremented from TIMx\_ARR to 0 or decremented from 0 to TIMxARR value without any index event, this is reported as an index position error.

The overflow threshold is programmed using the TIMx\_ARR register. A 1000 lines encoder results in a counter value being between 0 and 3999 (in 4x reading mode). The overflow detection threshold must be programmed by setting TIMx\_ARR = 3999 + 1 = 4000.

The error assertion is delayed to the transition 0 to 1 when in up-counting. This is to cope with narrow index pulses in gated A and B mode, as shown on [Figure 452](#XREF_65387__Figure_211__Error_detection41).

<a id="XREF_65387__Figure_211__Error_detection41"></a>

#### Figure 452. Up-counting encoder error detection![](MSv45780V1.svg)

In down-counting mode, the detection is conditioned by a preliminary transition from 1 to 0. This is to cope with narrow index pulses in gated A and B mode, as shown on [Figure 453](#XREF_61725__Figure_212__Encode_error_detection41), to avoid any false error detection in case the encoder dithers between TIMx\_ARR and 0 immediately after the index detection.

<a id="XREF_61725__Figure_212__Encode_error_detection41"></a>

#### Figure 453. Down-counting encode error detection![](MSv47416V1.svg)

An index error sets the IERRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. An index error interrupt is generated if the IERRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

#### Functional encoder interrupts

The following interrupts are also available in encoder mode

- Direction change: any change of the counting direction in encoder mode causes the DIR bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register to toggle. The direction change sets the DIRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. A direction change interrupt is generated if the DIRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.
- Index event: the index event sets the IDXF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. An index interrupt is generated if the IDXIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

#### Slave mode selection preload for run-time encoder mode update

It can be necessary to switch from one encoder mode to another during run-time. This is typically done at high-speed to decrease the update interrupt rate, by switching from x4 to x2 to x1 mode, as shown on [Figure 454](#XREF_73988__Figure_195__Encoder_mode_change_with_preload_enable41).

For this purpose, the SMS[3:0] bit can be preloaded. This is enabled by setting the SMSPE enable bit in the TIMx\_SMCR register. The trigger for the transfer from SMS[3:0] preload to active value can be selected with the SMSPS bit in the TIMx\_SMCR register.

- SMSPS = 0: the transfer is triggered by the update event (UEV) occurring when the counter overflows when up-counting, and underflows when down-counting. This mode must be used only when index is disabled (bit IE = 0).
- SMSPS = 1: the transfer is triggered by the index event.
<a id="XREF_73988__Figure_195__Encoder_mode_change_with_preload_enable41"></a>

#### Figure 454. Encoder mode change with preload transferred on update (SMSPS = 0)![](MSv45781V1.svg)

#### Encoder clock output

The encoder mode operating principle is not perfectly suited for high-resolution velocity measurements, at low speed, as it requires a relatively long integration time to have a sufficient number of clock edges and a precise measurement.

At low speed, a better solution is to do an edge-to-edge clock period measurement. This can be achieved using a slave timer. The timer can output the encoder clock information on the tim\_trgo output. The slave timer can then perform a period measurement and provide velocity information for each and every encoder clock edge.

This mode is enabled by setting the MMS[3:0] bitfield to 1000, in the TIMx\_CR2 register. It is valid for the following SMS[3:0] values: 0001, 0010, 0011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111. Any other SMS[3:0] code is not allowed and may lead to unexpected behavior.

### 30.4.19 Direction bit output

It is possible to output a direction signal out of the timer, on the tim\_oc3 and tim\_oc4 output signals (copy of the DIR bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register). This is achieved by setting the OC3M[3:0] or the OC4M[3:0] bitfield to 1011 in the TIMx\_CCMR2 register.

This feature can be used for monitoring the counting direction (or rotation direction) in encoder mode, or to have a signal indicating the up/down phases in center-aligned PWM mode.

### 30.4.20 UIF bit remapping

The IUFREMAP bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register forces a continuous copy of the update interrupt flag (UIF) into bit 31 of the timer counter register’s bit 31 (TIMxCNT[31]). This is used to atomically read both the counter value and a potential roll-over condition signaled by the UIFCPY flag. It eases the calculation of angular speed by avoiding race conditions caused, for instance, by a processing shared between a background task (counter reading) and an interrupt (update interrupt).

There is no latency between the UIF and UIFCPY flag assertions.

In 32-bit timer implementations, when the IUFREMAP bit is set, bit 31 of the counter is overwritten by the UIFCPY flag upon read access (the counter’s most significant bit is only accessible in write mode).

### 30.4.21 Timer input XOR function

The TI1S bit in the TIM1xx\_CR2 register, allows the input filter of channel 1 to be connected to the output of an XOR gate, combining the three input pins tim\_ti1, tim\_ti2 and tim\_ti3.

The XOR output can be used with all the timer input functions such as trigger or input capture.

An example of this feature used to interface Hall sensors is given in [Section 29.3.29: Interfacing with Hall sensors](Advanced-control_timers_%28TIM1__47_TIM8__47_TIM20%29.md#XREF_84491__15_4_16_Interfacing_with_Hall_sensors21).

### 30.4.22 Timers and external trigger synchronization

The TIMx timers can be synchronized with an external trigger in several modes: Reset mode, Gated mode, Trigger mode, Reset + trigger and gated + reset modes.

#### Slave mode: Reset mode

The counter and its prescaler can be reinitialized in response to an event on a trigger input. Moreover, if the URS bit from the TIMx\_CR1 register is low, an update event UEV is generated. Then all the preloaded registers (TIMx\_ARR, TIMx\_CCRx) are updated.

In the following example, the upcounter is cleared in response to a rising edge on tim\_ti1 input:

1. Configure the channel 1 to detect rising edges on tim\_ti1. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC1F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. The CC1S bits select the input capture source only, CC1S = 01 in the TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC1P = 0 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect rising edges only).
2. Configure the timer in reset mode by writing SMS = 100 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.
3. Start the counter by writing CEN = 1 in the TIMx\_CR1 register.

The counter starts counting on the internal clock, then behaves normally until tim\_ti1 rising edge. When tim\_ti1 rises, the counter is cleared and restarts from 0. In the meantime, the trigger flag is set (TIF bit in the TIMx\_SR register) and an interrupt request, or a DMA request can be sent if enabled (depending on the TIE and TDE bits in TIMx\_DIER register).

The following figure shows this behavior when the autoreload register TIMx\_ARR = 0x36. The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti1 and the actual reset of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti1 input.

#### Figure 455. Control circuit in reset mode![](MSv62361V1.svg)

#### Slave mode: Gated mode

The counter can be enabled depending on the level of a selected input.

In the following example, the upcounter counts only when tim\_ti1 input is low:

1. Configure the channel 1 to detect low levels on tim\_ti1. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC1F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. The CC1S bits select the input capture source only, CC1S = 01 in TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC1P = 1 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect low level only).
2. Configure the timer in gated mode by writing SMS = 101 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.
3. Enable the counter by writing CEN = 1 in the TIMx\_CR1 register (in gated mode, the counter does not start if CEN = 0, whatever is the trigger input level).

The counter starts counting on the internal clock as long as tim\_ti1 is low and stops as soon as tim\_ti1 becomes high. The TIF flag in the TIMx\_SR register is set both when the counter starts or stops.

The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti1 and the actual stop of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti1 input.

#### Figure 456. Control circuit in gated mode![](MSv62362V1.svg)

**Note:**

The configuration “CCxP = CCxNP = 1” (detection of both rising and falling edges) does not have any effect in gated mode because gated mode acts on a level and not on an edge.

#### Slave mode: Trigger mode

The counter can start in response to an event on a selected input.

In the following example, the upcounter starts in response to a rising edge on tim\_ti2 input:

1. Configure the channel 2 to detect rising edges on tim\_ti2. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC2F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. CC2S bits are selecting the input capture source only, CC2S = 01 in TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC2P = 1 and CC2NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect low level only).
2. Configure the timer in trigger mode by writing SMS = 110 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti2 as the input source by writing TS = 00110 in TIMx\_SMCR register.

When a rising edge occurs on tim\_ti2, the counter starts counting on the internal clock and the TIF flag is set.

The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti2 and the actual start of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti2 input.

#### Figure 457. Control circuit in trigger mode![](MSv62363V1.svg)

#### Slave mode selection preload for run-time encoder mode update

The SMS[3:0] bit can be preloaded. This is enabled by setting the SMSPE enable bit in the TIMx\_SMCR register. The trigger for the transfer from SMS[3:0] preload to active value is the update event (UEV) occurring when the counter overflows.

#### Slave mode – combined reset + trigger mode

In this case, a rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim\_trgi) reinitializes the counter, generates an update of the registers, and starts the counter.

This mode is used for one-pulse mode.

#### Slave mode – combined gated + reset mode

The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim\_trgi) is high. The counter stops and is reset as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.

This mode is used to detect out-of-range PWM signal (duty cycle exceeding a maximum expected value).

#### Slave mode – external clock mode 2 + trigger mode

The external clock mode 2 can be used in addition to another slave mode (except external clock mode 1 and encoder mode). In this case, the tim\_etr\_in signal is used as external clock input, and another input can be selected as trigger input when operating in reset mode, gated mode, or trigger mode. It is recommended not to select tim\_etr\_in as tim\_trgi through the TS bits of TIMx\_SMCR register.

In the following example, the upcounter is incremented at each rising edge of the tim\_etr\_in signal as soon as a rising edge of tim\_ti1 occurs:

1. Configure the external trigger input circuit by programming the TIMx\_SMCR register as follows:
<br>- ETF = 0000: no filter.
<br>- ETPS = 00: prescaler disabled.
<br>- ETP = 0: detection of rising edges on tim\_etr\_in and ECE = 1 to enable the external clock mode 2.
2. Configure the channel 1 as follows, to detect rising edges on TI:
<br>- IC1F = 0000: no filter.
<br>- The capture prescaler is not used for triggering and does not need to be configured.
<br>- CC1S = 01in TIMx\_CCMR1 register to select only the input capture source.
<br>- CC1P = 0 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect rising edge only).
3. Configure the timer in trigger mode by writing SMS = 110 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.

A rising edge on tim\_ti1 enables the counter and sets the TIF flag. The counter then counts on tim\_etr\_in rising edges.

The delay between the rising edge of the tim\_etr\_in signal and the actual reset of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_etrp input.

#### Figure 458. Control circuit in external clock mode 2 + trigger mode![](MSv62364V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_17049__12_4_14_Timer_synchronization41"></a>

### 30.4.23 Timer synchronization

The TIMx timers are linked together internally for timer synchronization or chaining. When one timer is configured in Master mode, it can reset, start, stop, or clock the counter of another timer configured in Slave mode.

[Figure 459](#XREF_16959__Figure_38__Master/Slave_Timer_Example41) and [Figure 460](#XREF_97482__Figure_434__Master/slave_connection_example_with_1_channel_onl41) show examples of master/slave timer connections.

#### Figure 459. Master/Slave timer example![](MSv62375V1.svg)

#### Figure 460. Master/slave connection example with 1 channel only timers![](MSv65225V1.svg)

**Note:**

The timers with one channel only (see [Figure 460](#XREF_97482__Figure_434__Master/slave_connection_example_with_1_channel_onl41)) do not feature a master mode. However, the tim\_oc1 output signal can serve as trigger for slave timer (see TIMx internal trigger connection table in [Section 30.4.2: TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5 pins and internal signals](#XREF_70970__28_4_2_TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5_pins_and_internal_signals41)).
The tim\_oc1 signal pulse width must be programmed to be at least two clock cycles of the destination timer, to make sure the slave timer detects the trigger.  
For instance, if the destination timer tim\_ker\_ck clock is four times slower than the source timer, the OC1 pulse width must be eight clock cycles.

<a id="XREF_26442__Using_another_timer_as_prescaler_for_the_PWM41"></a>

#### Using one timer as prescaler for another timer

For example, TIM\_mstr can be configured to act as a prescaler for TIM\_slv. Refer to [Figure 459](#XREF_16959__Figure_38__Master/Slave_Timer_Example41). To do this:

1. Configure TIM\_mstr in master mode so that it outputs a periodic trigger signal on each update event UEV. If MMS = 010 is written in the TIM\_mstr\_CR2 register, a rising edge is output on tim\_trgo each time an update event is generated.
2. To connect the tim\_trgo output of TIM\_mstr to TIM\_slv, TIM\_slv must be configured in slave mode using ITR2 as internal trigger. This is selected through the TS bits in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register (writing TS = 00010).
3. Then the slave mode controller must be put in external clock mode 1 (write SMS = 111 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register). This causes TIM\_slv to be clocked by the rising edge of the periodic TIM\_mstr trigger signal (which correspond to the TIM\_mstr counter overflow).
4. Finally both timers must be enabled by setting their respective CEN bits (TIMx\_CR1 register).

**Note:**

If tim\_ocx is selected on TIM\_mstr as the trigger output (MMS = 1xx), its rising edge is used to clock the counter of TIM\_slv.

#### Using one timer to enable another timer

In this example, we control the enable of TIM\_slv with the output compare 1 of TIM\_mstr. Refer to [Figure 459](#XREF_16959__Figure_38__Master/Slave_Timer_Example41) for connections. TIM\_slv counts on the divided internal clock only when tim\_oc1ref of TIM\_mstr is high. Both counter clock frequencies are divided by 3 by the prescaler compared to tim\_ker\_ck (ftim\_cnt\_ck = ftim\_ker\_ck/3).

1. Configure TIM\_mstr master mode to send its output compare 1 reference (tim\_oc1ref) signal as trigger output (MMS = 100 in the TIM\_mstr\_CR2 register).
2. Configure the TIM\_mstr tim\_oc1ref waveform (TIM\_mstr\_CCMR1 register).
3. Configure TIM\_slv to get the input trigger from TIM\_mstr (TS = 00010 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
4. Configure TIM\_slv in gated mode (SMS = 101 in TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
5. Enable TIM\_slv by writing 1 in the CEN bit (TIM\_slv\_CR1 register).
6. Start TIM\_mstr by writing 1 in the CEN bit (TIM\_mstr\_CR1 register).

**Note:**

The slave timer counter clock is not synchronized with the master timer counter clock, this mode only affects the TIM\_slv counter enable signal.

<a id="XREF_48726__Figure_192__Gating_TIM2_with_OC1REF_of_TIM141"></a>

#### Figure 461. Gating TIM\_slv with tim\_oc1ref of TIM\_mstr![MSv62376V1](MSv62376V1.svg)

In the example in [Figure 461](#XREF_48726__Figure_192__Gating_TIM2_with_OC1REF_of_TIM141), the TIM\_slv counter and prescaler are not initialized before being started. So they start counting from their current value. It is possible to start from a given value by resetting both timers before starting TIM\_mstr. Then any value can be written in the timer counters. The timers can easily be reset by software using the UG bit in the TIMx\_EGR registers.

In the next example (refer to [Figure 462](#XREF_50500__Figure_236__Gating_TIM2_with_Enable_of_TIM341)), we synchronize TIM\_mstr and TIM\_slv. TIM\_mstr is the master and starts from 0. TIM\_slv is the slave and starts from 0xE7. The prescaler ratio is the same for both timers. TIM\_slv stops when TIM\_mstr is disabled by writing 0 to the CEN bit in the TIM\_mstr\_CR1 register:

1. Configure TIM\_mstr master mode to send its output compare 1 reference (tim\_oc1ref) signal as trigger output (MMS = 100 in the TIM\_mstr\_CR2 register).
2. Configure the TIM\_mstr tim\_oc1ref waveform (TIM\_mstr\_CCMR1 register).
3. Configure TIM\_slv to get the input trigger from TIM\_mstr (TS = 00010 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
4. Configure TIM\_slv in gated mode (SMS = 101 in TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
5. Reset TIM\_mstr by writing 1 in UG bit (TIM\_mstr\_EGR register).
6. Reset TIM\_slv by writing 1 in UG bit (TIM\_slv\_EGR register).
7. Initialize TIM\_slv to 0xE7 by writing 0xE7 in the TIM\_slv counter (TIM\_slv\_CNT).
8. Enable TIM\_slv by writing 1 in the CEN bit (TIM\_slv\_CR1 register).
9. Start TIM\_mstr by writing 1 in the CEN bit (TIM\_mstr\_CR1 register).
10. Stop TIM\_mstr by writing 0 in the CEN bit (TIM\_mstr\_CR1 register).
<a id="XREF_50500__Figure_236__Gating_TIM2_with_Enable_of_TIM341"></a>

#### Figure 462. Gating TIM\_slv with Enable of TIM\_mstr![MSv62377V1](MSv62377V1.svg)

#### Using one timer to start another timer

In this example, we set the enable of TIM\_slv with the update event of TIM\_mstr. Refer to [Figure 459](#XREF_16959__Figure_38__Master/Slave_Timer_Example41) for connections. TIM\_slv starts counting from its current value (which can be nonzero) on the divided internal clock as soon as the update event is generated by TIM\_mstr. When TIM\_slv receives the trigger signal its CEN bit is automatically set and the counter counts until we write 0 to the CEN bit in the TIM\_slv\_CR1 register. Both counter clock frequencies are divided by 3 by the prescaler compared to tim\_ker\_ck (ftim\_cnt\_ck = ftim\_ker\_ck/3).

1. Configure TIM\_mstr master mode to send its update event (UEV) as trigger output (MMS = 010 in the TIM\_mstr\_CR2 register).
2. Configure the TIM\_mstr period (TIM\_mstr\_ARR registers).
3. Configure TIM\_slv to get the input trigger from TIM\_mstr (TS = 00010 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
4. Configure TIM\_slv in trigger mode (SMS = 110 in TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
5. Start TIM\_mstr by writing 1 in the CEN bit (TIM\_mstr\_CR1 register).
<a id="XREF_44696__Figure_47__Triggering_TIM2_with_update_of_TIM341"></a>

#### Figure 463. Triggering TIM\_slv with update of TIM\_mstr![](MSv62378V1.svg)

As in the previous example, both counters can be initialized before starting counting. [Figure 464](#XREF_64492__Figure_48__Triggering_TIM2_with_Enable_of_TIM341) shows the behavior with the same configuration as in [Figure 463](#XREF_44696__Figure_47__Triggering_TIM2_with_update_of_TIM341) but in trigger mode (SMS = 110 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register) instead of gated mode.

<a id="XREF_64492__Figure_48__Triggering_TIM2_with_Enable_of_TIM341"></a>

#### Figure 464. Triggering TIM\_slv with Enable of TIM\_mstr![](MSv62379V1.svg)

#### Starting two timers synchronously in response to an external trigger

In this example, we set the enable of TIM\_mstr when its tim\_ti1 input rises, and the enable of TIM\_slv with the enable of TIM\_mstr. Refer to [Figure 459](#XREF_16959__Figure_38__Master/Slave_Timer_Example41) for connections. To ensure the counters are aligned, TIM\_mstr must be configured in Master/Slave mode (slave with respect to tim\_ti1, master with respect to TIM\_slv):

1. Configure TIM\_mstr master mode to send its enable as trigger output (MMS = 001 in the TIM\_mstr\_CR2 register).
2. Configure TIM\_mstr slave mode to get the input trigger from tim\_ti1 (TS = 00100 in the TIM\_mstr\_SMCR register).
3. Configure TIM\_mstr in trigger mode (SMS = 110 in the TIM\_mstr\_SMCR register).
4. Configure the TIM\_mstr in Master/Slave mode by writing MSM = 1 (TIM\_mstr\_SMCR register).
5. Configure TIM\_slv to get the input trigger from TIM\_mstr (TS = 00000 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).
6. Configure TIM\_slv in trigger mode (SMS = 110 in the TIM\_slv\_SMCR register).

When a rising edge occurs on tim\_ti1 (TIM\_mstr), both counters start counting synchronously on the internal clock and both TIF flags are set.

**Note:**

In this example both timers are initialized before starting (by setting their respective UG bits). Both counters starts from 0, but an offset can easily be inserted between them by writing any of the counter registers (TIMx\_CNT). One can see that the master/slave mode inserts a delay between CNT\_EN and CK\_PSC on TIM\_mstr.

#### Figure 465. Triggering TIM\_mstr and TIM\_slv with TIM\_mstr tim\_ti1 input![](MSv62380V1.svg)

**Note:**

The clock of the slave peripherals (such as timer, ADC) receiving the tim\_trgo signal must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.

### 30.4.24 ADC triggers

The timer can generate an ADC triggering event with various internal signals, such as reset, enable or compare events.

**Note:**

The clock of the slave peripherals (such as timer, ADC) receiving the tim\_trgo signal must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.

### 30.4.25 DMA burst mode

The TIMx timers have the capability to generate multiple DMA requests upon a single event. The main purpose is to be able to reprogram part of the timer multiple times without software overhead, but it can also be used to read several registers in a row, at regular intervals.

The DMA controller destination is unique and must point to the virtual register TIMx\_DMAR. On a given timer event, the timer launches a sequence of DMA requests (burst). Each write into the TIMx\_DMAR register is actually redirected to one of the timer registers.

The DBL[4:0] bits in the TIMx\_DCR register set the DMA burst length. The timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx\_DMAR address), i.e. the number of transfers (either in half-words or in bytes).

The DBA[4:0] bits in the TIMx\_DCR registers define the DMA base address for DMA transfers (when read/write accesses are done through the TIMx\_DMAR address). DBA is defined as an offset starting from the address of the TIMx\_CR1 register:

Example:

00000: TIMx\_CR1

00001: TIMx\_CR2

00010: TIMx\_SMCR

As an example, the timer DMA burst feature is used to update the contents of the CCRx registers (x = 2, 3, 4) upon an update event, with the DMA transferring half words into the CCRx registers.

This is done in the following steps:

1. Configure the corresponding DMA channel as follows:
<br>- DMA channel peripheral address is the DMAR register address.
<br>- DMA channel memory address is the address of the buffer in the RAM containing the data to be transferred by DMA into CCRx registers.
<br>- Number of data to transfer = 3 (See note below).
<br>- Circular mode disabled.
2. Configure the DCR register by configuring the DBA and DBL bitfields as follows:
  DBL = 3 transfers, DBA = 0xE.
3. Enable the TIMx update DMA request (set the UDE bit in the DIER register).
4. Enable TIMx.
5. Enable the DMA channel.

This example is for the case where every CCRx register has to be updated once. If every CCRx register is to be updated twice for example, the number of data to transfer must be 6. Let's take the example of a buffer in the RAM containing data1, data2, data3, data4, data5, and data6. The data is transferred to the CCRx registers as follows: on the first update DMA request, data1 is transferred to CCR2, data2 is transferred to CCR3, data3 is transferred to CCR4 and on the second update DMA request, data4 is transferred to CCR2, data5 is transferred to CCR3, and data6 is transferred to CCR4.

**Note:**

A null value can be written to the reserved registers.

### 30.4.27 Debug mode

When the microcontroller enters debug mode (Cortex®-M4 with FPU core halted), the TIMx counter can either continue to work normally or stops.

The behavior in debug mode can be programmed with a dedicated configuration bit per timer in the Debug support (DBG) module.

For more details, refer to section Debug support (DBG).

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.87px"/><col width="497.40px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DITHEN</span>: Dithering Enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Dithering disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Dithering enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DITHEN bit can only be modified when CEN bit is reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIFREMAP</span>: UIF status bit remapping</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No remapping. UIF status bit is not copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.<br/>1: Remapping enabled. UIF status bit is copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKD[1:0]</span>: Clock division</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield indicates the division ratio between the timer clock (tim_ker_ck) frequency and sampling clock used by the digital filters (tim_etr_in, tim_tix),</p><p class="TableIndent">00: t<sub>DTS</sub> = t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>01: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 2 × t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>10: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 4 × t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>11: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ARPE</span>: Autoreload preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TIMx_ARR register is not buffered<br/>1: TIMx_ARR register is buffered</p></td></tr><tr height="218.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMS[1:0]</span>: Center-aligned mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Edge-aligned mode. The counter counts up or down depending on the direction bit (DIR).<br/>01: Center-aligned mode 1. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set only when the counter is counting down.<br/>10: Center-aligned mode 2. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set only when the counter is counting up.<br/>11: Center-aligned mode 3. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set both when the counter is counting up or down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>It is not allowed to switch from edge-aligned mode to center-aligned mode as long as the counter is enabled (CEN = 1)</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIR</span>: Direction</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter used as upcounter<br/>1: Counter used as downcounter</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is read only when the timer is configured in Center-aligned mode or Encoder mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPM</span>: One-pulse mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter is not stopped at update event<br/>1: Counter stops counting at the next update event (clearing the bit CEN)</p></td></tr><tr height="153.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">URS</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Update request source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select the UEV event sources.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Any of the following events generate an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled. These events can be: </p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Only counter overflow/underflow generates an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="169.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDIS</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Update disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable UEV event generation.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: UEV enabled. The Update (UEV) event is generated by one of the following events:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent">Buffered registers are then loaded with their preload values.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: UEV disabled. The Update event is not generated, shadow registers keep their value (ARR, PSC, CCRx). However the counter and the prescaler are reinitialized if the UG bit is set or if a hardware reset is received from the slave mode controller.</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CEN</span>: Counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter disabled<br/>1: Counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>External clock, gated mode and encoder mode can work only if the CEN bit has been previously set by software. However trigger mode can set the CEN bit automatically by hardware. </p><p class="TableBodyL">CEN is cleared automatically in one-pulse mode, when an update event occurs.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.2 TIMx control register 2 (TIMx\_CR2)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x004

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.77px"/><col width="497.58px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:<span data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0,_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3">26</span></p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="101.33px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ADSYNC</span>: ADC synchronization</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: The timer operates independently from the ADC</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 18.43pt;">1: The timer operation is synchronized with the ADC clock to provide jitter-free sampling point. This mode can be enabled only with specific ADC / timer clock relationship. Refer to <a href="#XREF_94361__47_4_25_ADC_synchronization" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 30.4.26</a> for requirements.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 18.43pt;">The ADSYNC must not modified when the counter is enabled (CEN bit is set).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 27:26</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="69.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TI1S</span>: tim_ti1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The tim_ti1_in[15:0] multiplexer output is to tim_ti1 input<br/>1: The tim_ti1_in[15:0], tim_ti2_in[15:0] and tim_ti3_in[15:0] multiplexers outputs are XORed and connected to the tim_ti1 input. See also <a href="Advanced-control_timers_%28TIM1__47_TIM8__47_TIM20%29.htm#XREF_84491__15_4_16_Interfacing_with_Hall_sensors21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.3.29: Interfacing with Hall sensors</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="466.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 25, 6, 5, 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MMS[3:0]</span>: Master mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are used to select the information to be sent in master mode to slave timers for synchronization (tim_trgo). The combination is as follows:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Reset</span> - the UG bit from the TIMx_EGR register is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). If the reset is generated by the trigger input (slave mode controller configured in reset mode) then the signal on tim_trgo is delayed compared to the actual reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Enable</span> - the Counter enable signal, CNT_EN, is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). It is useful to start several timers at the same time or to control a window in which a slave timer is enabled. The Counter Enable signal is generated by a logic AND between CEN control bit and the trigger input when configured in gated mode.<br/>When the Counter Enable signal is controlled by the trigger input, there is a delay on tim_trgo, except if the master/slave mode is selected (see the MSM bit description in TIMx_SMCR register).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Update</span> - The update event is selected as trigger output (tim_trgo). For instance a master timer can then be used as a prescaler for a slave timer.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare Pulse</span> - The trigger output send a positive pulse when the CC1IF flag is to be set (even if it was already high), as soon as a capture or a compare match occurred (tim_trgo).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc1refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc2refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc3refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc4refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000: <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Encoder clock output</span> - The encoder clock signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). This code is valid for the following SMS[3:0] values: 0001, 0010, 0011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111. Any other SMS[3:0] code is not allowed and may lead to unexpected behavior.</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock of the slave timer or ADC must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCDS</span>: Capture/compare DMA selection</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CCx DMA request sent when CCx event occurs<br/>1: CCx DMA requests sent when update event occurs</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.3 TIMx slave mode control register (TIMx\_SMCR)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x008

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.40px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMSPS</span>: SMS preload source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether the events that triggers the SMS[3:0] bitfield transfer from preload to active</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The transfer is triggered by the Timer’s Update event</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The transfer is triggered by the Index event</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMSPE</span>: SMS preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether the SMS[3:0] bitfield is preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">0: SMS[3:0] bitfield is not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">1: SMS[3:0] preload is enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETP</span>: External trigger polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether tim_etr_in or <span style="text-decoration: overline;">tim_etr_in</span> is used for trigger operations </p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_etr_in is non-inverted, active at high level or rising edge<br/>1: tim_etr_in is inverted, active at low level or falling edge</p></td></tr><tr height="190.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECE</span>: External clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables External clock mode 2.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: External clock mode 2 disabled<br/>1: External clock mode 2 enabled. The counter is clocked by any active edge on the tim_etrf signal.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Setting the ECE bit has the same effect as selecting external clock mode 1 with tim_trgi connected to tim_etrf (SMS = 111 and TS = 00111).<br/>It is possible to simultaneously use external clock mode 2 with the following slave modes: reset mode, gated mode and trigger mode. Nevertheless, tim_trgi must not be connected to tim_etrf in this case (TS bits must not be 00111).<br/>If external clock mode 1 and external clock mode 2 are enabled at the same time, the external clock input is tim_etrf.</p></td></tr><tr height="129.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETPS[1:0]</span>: External trigger prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">External trigger signal tim_etrp frequency must be at most 1/4 of tim_ker_ck frequency. A prescaler can be enabled to reduce tim_etrp frequency. It is useful when inputting fast external clocks on tim_etr_in.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Prescaler OFF<br/>01: tim_etrp frequency divided by 2<br/>10: tim_etrp frequency divided by 4<br/>11: tim_etrp frequency divided by 8</p></td></tr><tr height="305.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETF[3:0]</span>: External trigger filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield then defines the frequency used to sample tim_etrp signal and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_etrp. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N consecutive events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: No filter, sampling is done at f<sub>DTS<br/></sub>0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2<br/>0010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4<br/>0011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 8<br/>0100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 6<br/>0101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 8<br/>0110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 6<br/>0111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 8<br/>1000:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6<br/>1001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8<br/>1010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5<br/>1011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6<br/>1100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8<br/>1101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5<br/>1110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6<br/>1111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MSM</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Master/Slave mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: The effect of an event on the trigger input (tim_trgi) is delayed to allow a perfect synchronization between the current timer and its slaves (through tim_trgo). It is useful if we want to synchronize several timers on a single external event.</p></td></tr><tr height="438.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21, 20, 6, 5, 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TS[4:0]</span>: Trigger selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield selects the trigger input to be used to synchronize the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: Internal trigger 0 (tim_itr0)</p><p class="TableIndent">00001: Internal trigger 1 (tim_itr1)</p><p class="TableIndent">00010: Internal trigger 2 (tim_itr2)</p><p class="TableIndent">00011: Internal trigger 3 (tim_itr3)</p><p class="TableIndent">00100: tim_ti1 edge detector (tim_ti1f_ed)</p><p class="TableIndent">00101: Filtered timer input 1 (tim_ti1fp1)</p><p class="TableIndent">00110: Filtered timer input 2 (tim_ti2fp2)</p><p class="TableIndent">00111: External trigger input (tim_etrf)</p><p class="TableIndent">01000: Internal trigger 4 (tim_itr4)</p><p class="TableIndent">01001: Internal trigger 5 (tim_itr5)</p><p class="TableIndent">01010: Internal trigger 6 (tim_itr6)</p><p class="TableIndent">01011: Internal trigger 7 (tim_itr7)</p><p class="TableIndent">01100: Internal trigger 8 (tim_itr8)</p><p class="TableIndent">01101: Internal trigger 9 (tim_itr9)</p><p class="TableIndent">01110: Internal trigger 10 (tim_itr10)</p><p class="TableIndent">01111: Internal trigger 11 (tim_itr11)</p><p class="TableIndent">10000: Internal trigger 12 (tim_itr12)</p><p class="TableIndent">10001: Internal trigger 13 (tim_itr13)</p><p class="TableIndent">10010: Internal trigger 14 (tim_itr14)</p><p class="TableIndent">10011: Internal trigger 15 (tim_itr15)</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent">See <a href="#XREF_70970__28_4_2_TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5_pins_and_internal_signals41" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 30.4.2: TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5 pins and internal signals</a> for product specific implementation details.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits must be changed only when they are not used (for example when SMS = 000) to avoid wrong edge detections at the transition.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">OCCS</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> OCREF clear selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used to select the OCREF clear source</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_ocref_clr_int is connected to the tim_ocref_clr input</p><p class="TableIndent">1: tim_ocref_clr_int is connected to tim_etrf</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the OCREF clear selection feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and forced by hardware to 0. <a href="#XREF_40020__28_3_TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5_implementation41" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 30.3: TIM2/TIM3/TIM4/TIM5 implementation</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="668.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 2, 1, 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMS[3:0]</span>: Slave mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">When external signals are selected the active edge of the trigger signal (tim_trgi) is linked to the polarity selected on the external input (refer to ETP bit in TIMx_SMCR for tim_etr_in and CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIMx_CCER register for tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0000:   Slave mode disabled - if CEN = 1 then the prescaler is clocked directly by the internal clock.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0001:   Encoder mode 1 - Counter counts up/down on tim_ti1fp1 edge depending on tim_ti2fp2 level.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0010:   Encoder mode 2 - Counter counts up/down on tim_ti2fp2 edge depending on tim_ti1fp1 level.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0011:   Encoder mode 3 - Counter counts up/down on both tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2 edges depending on the level of the other input.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0100:   Reset mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter and generates an update of the registers.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0101:   Gated mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops (but is not reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0110:   Trigger mode - The counter starts at a rising edge of the trigger tim_trgi (but it is not reset). Only the start of the counter is controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">0111:   External clock mode 1 - Rising edges of the selected trigger (tim_trgi) clock the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1000:   Combined reset + trigger mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter, generates an update of the registers and starts the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1001:   Combined gated + reset mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops and is reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1010:   Encoder mode: Clock plus direction, x2 mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1011:   Encoder mode: Clock plus direction, x1 mode, tim_ti2fp2 edge sensitivity is set by CC2P.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1100:   Encoder mode: Directional clock, x2 mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1101:   Encoder mode: Directional clock, x1 mode, tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2 edge sensitivity is set by CC1P and CC2P.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1110:   Quadrature encoder mode: x1 mode, counting on tim_ti1fp1 edges only, edge sensitivity is set by CC1P.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 32.60pt;">1111:   Quadrature encoder mode: x1 mode, counting on tim_ti2fp2 edges only, edge sensitivity is set by CC2P.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The gated mode must not be used if tim_ti1f_ed is selected as the trigger input (TS = 00100). Indeed, tim_ti1f_ed outputs 1 pulse for each transition on tim_ti1f, whereas the gated mode checks the level of the trigger signal.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock of the slave peripherals (such as timer, ADC) receiving the tim_trgo signal must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.4 TIMx DMA/Interrupt enable register (TIMx\_DIER)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x00C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.01px"/><col width="500.16px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TERRF</span>: Transition error interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when a transition error is detected in encoder mode. It is cleared</p><p class="TableIndent">by software by writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No encoder transition error has been detected.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: An encoder transition error has been detected</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IERRF</span>: Index error interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when an index error is detected. It is cleared by software by</p><p class="TableIndent">writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No index error has been detected.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: An index error has been detected</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIRF</span>: Direction change interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when the direction changes in encoder mode (DIR bit value in</p><p class="TableIndent">TIMx_CR is changing). It is cleared by software by writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No direction change</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Direction change</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDXF</span>: Index interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when an index event is detected. It is cleared by software by</p><p class="TableIndent">writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No index event occurred.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: An index event has occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4OF</span>: Capture/Compare 4 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3OF</span>: Capture/Compare 3 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2OF</span>: Capture/compare 2 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1OF</span>: Capture/Compare 1 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware only when the corresponding channel is configured in input capture mode. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No overcapture has been detected.<br/>1: The counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register while CC1IF flag was already set</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 8:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="98.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TIF</span>: Trigger interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on the TRG trigger event (active edge detected on tim_trgi input) when the slave mode controller is enabled in all modes but gated mode. It is set when the counter starts or stops when gated mode is selected. It is cleared by software.<br/>0: No trigger event occurred.<br/>1: Trigger interrupt pending.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4IF</span>: Capture/Compare 4 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3IF</span>: Capture/Compare 3 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2IF</span>: Capture/Compare 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="221.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1IF</span>: Capture/compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware. It is cleared by software (input capture or output compare mode) or by reading the TIMx_CCR1 register (input capture mode only).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No compare match / No input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A compare match or an input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>: this flag is set when the content of the counter TIMx_CNT matches the content of the TIMx_CCR1 register. When the content of TIMx_CCR1 is greater than the content of TIMx_ARR, the CC1IF bit goes high on the counter overflow (in up-counting and up/down-counting modes) or underflow (in down-counting mode). There are three possible options for flag setting in center-aligned mode, refer to the CMS bits in the TIMx_CR1 register for the full description.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>: this bit is set when counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register (an edge has been detected on IC1, as per the edge sensitivity defined with the CC1P and CC1NP bits setting, in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIF</span>: Update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware on an update event. It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No update occurred<br/>1: Update interrupt pending. This bit is set by hardware when the registers are updated:</p><p class="TableIndent">At overflow or underflow and if UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When CNT is reinitialized by software using the UG bit in TIMx_EGR register, if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When CNT is reinitialized by a trigger event (refer to the synchro control register description), if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.6 TIMx event generation register (TIMx\_EGR)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x014

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.76px"/><col width="499.42px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TG</span>: Trigger generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: The TIF flag is set in TIMx_SR register. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4G</span>: Capture/compare 4 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3G</span>: Capture/compare 3 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2G</span>: Capture/compare 2 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="173.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1G</span>: Capture/compare 1 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: A capture/compare event is generated on channel 1:<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>:<br/>CC1IF flag is set, Corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>:<br/>The current value of the counter is captured in TIMx_CCR1 register. The CC1IF flag is set, the corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled. The CC1OF flag is set if the CC1IF flag was already high.</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UG</span>: Update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: Re-initialize the counter and generates an update of the registers. Note that the prescaler counter is cleared too (anyway the prescaler ratio is not affected). The counter is cleared if the center-aligned mode is selected or if DIR = 0 (up-counting), else it takes the autoreload value (TIMx_ARR) if DIR = 1 (down-counting).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.7 TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 (TIMx\_CCMR1)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x018

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).
