<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.19px"/><col width="499.99px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC2F[3:0]</span>: Input capture 2 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC2PSC[1:0]</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Input capture 2 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 2 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC2 channel is configured as output.<br/>01: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti2.<br/>10: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti1.<br/>11: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="325.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC1F[3:0]</span>: Input capture 1 filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample tim_ti1 input and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_ti1. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N consecutive events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   No filter, sampling is done at f<sub>DTS</sub></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC1PSC[1:0]</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Input capture 1 prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the ratio of the prescaler acting on CC1 input (tim_ic1). The prescaler is reset as soon as CC1E = 0 (TIMx_CCER register).</p><p class="TableIndent">00: no prescaler, capture is done each time an edge is detected on the capture input<br/>01: capture is done once every 2 events<br/>10: capture is done once every 4 events<br/>11: capture is done once every 8 events</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC1 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1<br/>10: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2<br/>11: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.8 TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 [alternate]    (TIMx\_CCMR1)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x018

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="494.40px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2CE</span>: Output compare 2 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24, 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 2 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">refer to OC1M description on bits 6:4</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2PE</span>: Output compare 2 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2FE</span>: Output compare 2 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 2 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC2 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti2<br/>10: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti1<br/>11: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through the TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1CE</span>: Output compare 1 clear enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr_int input<br/>1: tim_oc1ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr_int input</p></td></tr><tr height="753.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 1 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc1ref from which tim_oc1 is derived. tim_oc1ref is active high whereas tim_oc1 active level depends on CC1P bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000: Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIMx_CCR1 and the counter TIMx_CNT has no effect on the outputs. This mode can be used when the timer serves as a software timebase. When the frozen mode is enabled during timer operation, the ouput keeps the state (active or inactive) it had before entering the frozen state.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001: Set channel 1 to active level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced high when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010: Set channel 1 to inactive level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced low when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011: Toggle - tim_oc1ref toggles when TIMx_CNT = TIMx_CCR1.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100: Force inactive level - tim_oc1ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101: Force active level - tim_oc1ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110: PWM mode 1 - In up-counting, channel 1 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else inactive. In down-counting, channel 1 is inactive (tim_oc1ref = 0) as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR1 else active (tim_oc1ref = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111: PWM mode 2 - In up-counting, channel 1 is inactive as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else active. In down-counting, channel 1 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR1 else inactive.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000: Retriggerable OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001: Retriggerable OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010: Reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011: Reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100: Combined PWM mode 1 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc1refc is the logical OR between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101: Combined PWM mode 2 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc1refc is the logical AND between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110: Asymmetric PWM mode 1 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc1refc outputs tim_oc1ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc2ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111: Asymmetric PWM mode 2 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc1refc outputs tim_oc1ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc2ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes when the result of the comparison changes, when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode and when the output compare mode switches from “force active/inactive” mode to “PWM” mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1PE</span>: Output compare 1 preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 disabled. TIMx_CCR1 can be written at anytime, the new value is taken in account immediately.<br/>1: Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload register. TIMx_CCR1 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.</p></td></tr><tr height="173.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1FE</span>: Output compare 1 fast enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIMx_CR1 register), to have the output pulse starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CC1 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR1 values even when the trigger is ON. The minimum delay to activate CC1 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input is 5 clock cycles.<br/>1: An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC1 output. Then, OC is set to the compare level independently from the result of the comparison. Delay to sample the trigger input and to activate CC1 output is reduced to three clock cycles. OCFE acts only if the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC1 channel is configured as output.<br/>01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1.<br/>10: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2.<br/>11: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.9 TIMx capture/compare mode register 2 (TIMx\_CCMR2)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x01C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Input capture mode

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="116.74px"/><col width="497.43px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC4F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 4 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC4PSC[1:0]</span>: Input capture 4 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 4 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC4 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>10: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>11: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC4S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC4E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC3F[3:0]</span>: Input capture 3 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC3PSC[1:0]</span>: Input capture 3 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 3 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC3 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>10: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>11: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC3S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC3E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.10 TIMx capture/compare mode register 2 [alternate]    (TIMx\_CCMR2)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x01C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.67px"/><col width="498.50px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4CE</span>: Output compare 4 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24, 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 4 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to OC3M[3:0]</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4PE</span>: Output compare 4 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4FE</span>: Output compare 4 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 4 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC4 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>10: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>11: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC4S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC4E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3CE</span>: Output compare 3 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="817.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 3 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc3ref from which tim_oc3 and tim_oc3n are derived. tim_oc3ref is active high whereas tim_oc3 and tim_oc3n active level depends on CC3P and CC3NP bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIMx_CCR3 and the counter TIMx_CNT has no effect on the outputs.(this mode is used to generate a timing base).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Set channel 3 to active level on match. tim_oc3ref signal is forced high when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 3 (TIMx_CCR3).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Set channel 3 to inactive level on match. tim_oc3ref signal is forced low when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 3 (TIMx_CCR3).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Toggle - tim_oc3ref toggles when TIMx_CNT = TIMx_CCR3.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Force inactive level - tim_oc3ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Force active level - tim_oc3ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   PWM mode 1 - In up-counting, channel 3 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR3 else inactive. In down-counting, channel 3 is inactive (tim_oc3ref = 0) as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR3 else active (tim_oc3ref = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   PWM mode 2 - In up-counting, channel 3 is inactive as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR3 else active. In down-counting, channel 3 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR3 else inactive.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   Pulse on compare: a pulse is generated on tim_oc3ref upon CCR3 match event, as per PWPRSC[2:0] and PW[7:0] bitfields programming in TIMxECR.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   Direction output. The tim_oc3ref signal is overridden by a copy of the DIR bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   Combined PWM mode 1 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc3refc is the logical OR between tim_oc3ref and tim_oc4ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101: Combined PWM mode 2 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc3refc is the logical AND between tim_oc3ref and tim_oc4ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   Asymmetric PWM mode 1 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc3refc outputs tim_oc3ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc4ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   Asymmetric PWM mode 2 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc3refc outputs tim_oc3ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc4ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes only when the result of the comparison changes or when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode.</p><p class="TableBodyL">On channels having a complementary output, this bitfield is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the OC3M active bits take the new value from the preloaded bits only when a COM event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3PE</span>: Output compare 3 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3FE</span>: Output compare 3 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 3 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC3 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>10: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>11: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC3S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC3E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.11 TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx\_CCER)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x020

Reset value: 0x0000

2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="297.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1P</span>: <span style="font-style:Italic;">Capture/Compare 1 output Polarity.</span></p><p class="TableIndent">0: OC1 active high (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: OC1 active low (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">When CC1 channel is configured as input, both CC1NP/CC1P bits select the active polarity of TI1FP1 and TI2FP1 for trigger or capture operations.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 102.05pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 0:   non-inverted/rising edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 rising edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode or encoder mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 102.05pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 1:   inverted/falling edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 falling edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is inverted (trigger operation in gated mode or encoder mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 102.05pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 1:   non-inverted/both edges. The circuit is sensitive to both TIxFP1 rising and falling edges (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode). This configuration must not be used in encoder mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 102.05pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 0:   this configuration is reserved, it must not be used.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1E</span>: <span style="font-style:Italic;">Capture/Compare 1 output enable.</span></p><p class="TableIndent">0: Capture mode disabled / OC1 is not active</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-kerning:none;">1: Capture mode enabled / OC1 signal is output on the corresponding output pin</p></td></tr></table></div>


 


<div align="center"><table class="TableTitle"><caption class="~TableHeading"><h4 class="TableCap" id="1020299">Table 301. <a id="channels%1141" name="XREF_87292__Table_304__Output_control_bit_for_standard_tim_ocx_channels%1141">Output control bit for standard tim_ocx channels</a></h4></caption><col width="95.96px"/><col width="441.73px"/><thead><tr height="22.67px"><th><p class="TableBodyC"><a id="1020303" name="336_TableBodyC_1020303"></a>CCxE bit</p></th><th><p class="TableBodyL">tim_ocx output state</p></th></tr></thead><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="TableBodyC">0</p></td><td><p class="TableIndent">Output disabled (not driven by the timer: Hi-Z)</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="TableBodyC">1</p></td><td><p class="TableIndent">Output enabled (tim_ocx = tim_ocxref + Polarity)</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

The state of the external IO pins connected to the standard tim\_ocx channels depends only on the GPIO registers when CCxE = 0.

### 30.5.12 TIMx counter (TIMx\_CNT)(x = 3, 4)

Address offset: 0x024

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_16bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR1[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR1 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 1 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR1 register (bit OC1PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 1 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc1 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR1 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic1). The TIMx_CCR1 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The CCR1[15:0] bits hold the capture value. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR1[19:0]. The CCR1[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.18 TIMx capture/compare register 1 (TIMx\_CCR1)(x = 2, 5)

Address offset: 0x034

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_32bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR1[31:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR1 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 1 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR1 register (bit OC1PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 1 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc1 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR1[31:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR1 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic1). The TIMx_CCR1 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR1[31:0]. The CCR1[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.19 TIMx capture/compare register 2 (TIMx\_CCR2)(x = 3, 4)

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_16bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR2[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 2 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR2 register (bit OC2PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 2 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc2 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR2[15:0]. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR2[19:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 2 event (tim_ic2). The TIMx_CCR2 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The CCR2[15:0] bits hold the capture value. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR2[19:0]. The CCR2[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.20 TIMx capture/compare register 2 (TIMx\_CCR2)(x = 2, 5)

Address offset: 0x038

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_32bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR2[31:0]</span>: Capture/compare 2 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 2 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR2 register (bit OC2PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 2 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc2 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR2[31:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 2 event (tim_ic2). The TIMx_CCR2 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR2[31:0]. The CCR2[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.21 TIMx capture/compare register 3 (TIMx\_CCR3)(x = 3, 4)

Address offset: 0x03C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_16bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR3[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 3 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR3 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 3 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR3 register (bit OC3PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 3 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc3 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR3[15:0]. The CCR3[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR3[19:4]. The CCR3[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR3 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 3 event (tim_ic3). The TIMx_CCR3 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The CCR3[15:0] bits hold the capture value. The CCR3[19:16] bits are reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR3[19:0]. The CCR3[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.22 TIMx capture/compare register 3 (TIMx\_CCR3)(x = 2, 5)

Address offset: 0x03C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_32bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR3[31:0]</span>: Capture/compare 3 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR3 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 3 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR3 register (bit OC3PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 3 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc3 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR3[31:4]. The CCR3[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR3 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 3 event (tim_ic3). The TIMx_CCR3 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR3[31:0]. The CCR3[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.23 TIMx capture/compare register 4 (TIMx\_CCR4)(x = 3, 4)

Address offset: 0x040

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_16bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR4[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 4 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR4 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 4 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR4 register (bit OC4PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 4 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc4 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR4[15:0]. The CCR4[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR4[19:4]. The CCR4[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR4 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 4 event (tim_ic4). The TIMx_CCR4 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The CCR4[15:0] bits hold the capture value. The CCR4[19:16] bits are reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR4[19:0]. The CCR4[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.24 TIMx capture/compare register 4 (TIMx\_CCR4)(x = 2, 5)

Address offset: 0x040

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_32bit"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.02px"/><col width="499.16px"/><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR4[31:0]</span>: Capture/compare 4 value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR4 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 4 register (preload value). It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR4 register (bit OC4PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 4 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc4 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR4[31:4]. The CCR4[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR4 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 4 event (tim_ic4). The TIMx_CCR4 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR4[31:0]. The CCR4[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.25 TIMx timer encoder control register (TIMx\_ECR)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x058

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 26:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PWPRSC[2:0]</span>: Pulse width prescaler</p><p class="Body">This bitfield sets the clock prescaler for the pulse generator, as following:</p><p class="Body">t<sub>PWG</sub> = (2<sup>(PWPRSC[2:0])</sup>) x <span style="font-size : 9.00pt;">t</span><sub><span style="font-size : 9.00pt;">tim_ker_ck</span></sub></p></td></tr><tr height="64.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PW[7:0]</span>: Pulse width</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the pulse duration, as following:</p><p class="Body">t<sub>PW</sub> = PW[7:0] x t<sub>PWG</sub></p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="233.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IPOS[1:0]</span>: Index positioning</p><p class="TableBodyL">In quadrature encoder mode (SMS[3:0] = 0001, 0010, 0011, 1110, 1111), this bit indicates in which AB input configuration the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index resets the counter when AB = 00</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index resets the counter when AB = 01</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index resets the counter when AB = 10</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Index resets the counter when AB = 11</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableBodyL">In directional clock mode or clock plus direction mode (SMS[3:0] = 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101), these bits indicates on which level the Index event resets the counter. In bidirectional clock mode, this applies for both clock inputs.</p><p class="TableIndent">x0: Index resets the counter when clock is 0</p><p class="TableIndent">x1: Index resets the counter when clock is 1</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>IPOS[1] bit is not significant</p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FIDX</span>: First index </p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the first index only is taken into account</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Index is always active</p><p class="TableIndent">1: the first Index only resets the counter</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0,_gpt2gcv4_1" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0,_gpt2gcv4_1"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0,_gpt2gcv4_1"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="105.33px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IBLK[1:0]</span>: Index blanking</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the Index event is conditioned by the tim_ti3 input</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index always active</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index disabled hen tim_ti3 input is active, as per CC3P bitfield</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index disabled when tim_ti4 input is active, as per CC4P bitfield</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="122.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDIR[1:0]</span>: Index direction</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates in which direction the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index resets the counter whatever the direction</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index resets the counter when up-counting only</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index resets the counter when down-counting only</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span><span data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0,_gpt2gcv4_1">The IDR[1:0] bitfield must be written when IE bit is reset (index disabled).</span></p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IE</span>: Index enable</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Index disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Index enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.26 TIMx timer input selection register (TIMx\_TISEL)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x05C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.77px"/><col width="499.41px"/><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:13</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_0"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="244.00px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:16</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBSS[3:0]</span>: DMA burst source selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the interrupt source that triggers the DMA burst transfers (the timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx_DMAR address).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;"><span data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv4_dma1_dma2,_gpt2gcv5_0">0000: Legacy mode. Any source triggers the transfer. It is possible to combine several interrupt sources for triggering DMA burst transfers.</span></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001: Update</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010: CC1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011: CC2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100: CC3</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101: CC4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110: COM</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111: Trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: reserved</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:13</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2gcv4_1,_gpt2gcv4_2,_gpt2gcv4_3,_gpt2gcv4_4,_gpt2gcv4_5,_gpt2gcv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="349.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 12:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBL[4:0]</span>: DMA burst length</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bit vector defines the length of DMA transfers (the timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx_DMAR address), i.e. the number of transfers. Transfers can be in half-words or in bytes (see example below).</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: 1 transfer<br/>00001: 2 transfers<br/>00010: 3 transfers<br/>...<br/>11010: 26 transfers</p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Example:</span> Let us consider the following transfer: DBL = 7 bytes &amp; DBA = TIM2_CR1.</p><li class="TableBullet" id="10299606" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If DBL = 7 bytes and DBA = TIM2_CR1 represents the address of the byte to be transferred, the address of the transfer is given by the following equation:</li><p class="TableIndent">(TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA + (DMA index), where DMA index = DBL</p><p class="TableIndent">In this example, 7 bytes are added to (TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA, which gives us the address from/to which the data are copied. In this case, the transfer is done to 7 registers starting from the following address: (TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA</p><p class="TableIndent">According to the configuration of the DMA Data Size, several cases may occur:</p><li class="TableBullet" id="10299610" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If the DMA Data Size is configured in half-words, 16-bit data are transferred to each of the 7 registers.</li><li class="TableBullet" id="10299611" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If the DMA Data Size is configured in bytes, the data are also transferred to 7 registers: the first register contains the first MSB byte, the second register, the first LSB byte and so on. So with the transfer Timer, one also has to specify the size of data transferred by DMA.</li></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="144.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBA[4:0]</span>: DMA base address</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bits vector defines the base-address for DMA transfers (when read/write access are done through the TIMx_DMAR address). DBA is defined as an offset starting from the address of the TIMx_CR1 register.<br/>Example:</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: TIMx_CR1,<br/>00001: TIMx_CR2,<br/>00010: TIMx_SMCR,<br/>...</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 30.5.30 TIMx DMA address for full transfer (TIMx\_DMAR)(x = 2 to 5)

Address offset: 0x3E0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAB[31:0]</span>: DMA register for burst accesses</p><p class="TableIndent">A read or write operation to the DMAR register accesses the register located at the address</p><p class="TableBodyC">(TIMx_CR1 address) + (DBA + DMA index) x 4 </p><p class="TableIndent">where TIMx_CR1 address is the address of the control register 1, DBA is the DMA base address configured in TIMx_DCR register, DMA index is automatically controlled by the DMA transfer, and ranges from 0 to DBL (DBL configured in TIMx_DCR).</p></td></tr></table></div>
